title: Automorphism twists of curves and compatible homeomorphic endomorphism lifts
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $a:C\to S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be a smooth proper integral curve of dimension one [def-kun-dimension], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-sc-curves], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $\sigma:k\xrightarrow{\sim}k$ be a field automorphism (a bijective unital field homomorphism), put $s=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$, and form $T=C\times_{S,s}S$ with projections $\pi:T\to C$ and $b:T\to S$ [def-pc-base-change], [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $a$ and $b$ are smooth of relative dimension one, $T$ is a smooth proper integral $k$-curve of dimension one, and $\pi$ is an isomorphism of schemes with inverse $(\operatorname{id}_C,s^{-1}a)$.
For any scheme endomorphism $u:C\to C$ satisfying $au=sa$ and inducing a homeomorphism on underlying topological spaces, there is a unique $k$-morphism $v:C\to T$ with $\pi v=u$ and $bv=a$. It is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces, sends generic point to generic point [def-sc-generic-point], and does not factor through a $k$-rational point of $T$. On function fields [def-sc-function-field], its pullback (the generic stalk homomorphism) is injective and, writing $\beta=\pi^*:k(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(T)$, one has $v^*\beta=u^*$. No $k$-linearity is asserted for $\pi$, $\beta$ or $u^*$. If $\sigma=\operatorname{id}_k$ and $u=\operatorname{id}_C$, then $\pi v=\operatorname{id}_C$ identifies $v$ with the identity under the canonical identity-base-change identification.

proof.text: By functoriality of Spec, $s^{-1}=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma^{-1})$. The relation $a\pi=sb$ gives $s^{-1}a\pi=b$. The fibre-product universal property therefore gives $j=(\operatorname{id}_C,s^{-1}a):C\to T$. Its first projection is $\pi j=\operatorname{id}_C$. The two projections of $j\pi$ are $\pi$ and $s^{-1}a\pi=b$, so uniqueness gives $j\pi=\operatorname{id}_T$. Thus $\pi$ is an isomorphism with precisely the asserted inverse.

source.place: Tag 0CCG (remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius), Cartesian diagram, with the automorphism refinement proved here

proof.text: The given $C$ is an integral separated finite-type curve of dimension one over $k$, so [lem-sc-curve-base-change-relative-dimension-one] applies. For the identity base map, the projection $q:C\times_S S\to C$ has inverse $(\operatorname{id}_C,a)$ by the two projection equations, and its structure map is $aq$. Thus the lemma gives relative dimension one for $a$: the identified fibres have identical open sets and hence the same local dimensions. For the base map $s$, the lemma directly gives that $b$ is smooth of relative dimension one. Properness of $a$ and [lem-pc-proper-base-change](1) give properness of $b$, which includes separatedness and finite type. The isomorphism $\pi$ identifies affine opens and their section rings; hence the domain condition defining integrality of $C$ holds for every nonempty affine open of $T$, and $T$ is nonempty. Its underlying homeomorphism identifies chains of irreducible closed subsets, so $\dim T=\dim C=1$. This proves all the claimed curve properties.

source.place: Tag 0CCY (lemma-inseparable-deg-p-smooth), first proof paragraph; geometric inputs Tags 01W4, 01VB, 02NK and 0A21(3)

proof.text: The equality $au=sa$ is exactly the compatibility required to form $v=(u,a):C\to T$. The universal property gives $\pi v=u$ and $bv=a$, and says that these equations determine $v$ uniquely. The second equation is the definition of being a morphism over $k$. Composing the first equation with $j$ gives $v=ju$. Thus on underlying spaces $|v|=|j|\circ|u|$, a composite of homeomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0CCG (remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius), Cartesian diagram, with the automorphism refinement proved here

proof.text: An integral scheme is irreducible, and [lem-sc-scheme-sober] gives its unique generic point. A homeomorphism takes the closure of a singleton onto the closure of its image singleton. Applying this to $u$, $\pi$, and $v$ shows that each sends the unique generic point to the unique generic point. If $v$ factored as $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k\xrightarrow{t}T$ for a $k$-rational point $t$, its image would be a singleton, since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has one point. Surjectivity of $|v|$ would make $|T|$ a singleton; every nonempty irreducible closed-subset chain would then have length zero, contradicting $\dim T=1$. Hence the asserted nonconstancy holds.

source.place: Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober), and the definitions of generic point and topological dimension

proof.text: Use $k(C)=\mathcal O_{C,\eta_C}$ and $k(T)=\mathcal O_{T,\eta_T}$, which are fields by [def-sc-function-field]. Since the maps preserve generic points, pullback of a section on a neighbourhood followed by passage to its germ defines unital homomorphisms $u^*$, $v^*$ and $\beta=\pi^*$ between these fields. Pullbacks commute with restrictions, so these germ maps are well defined. On a germ represented by a section $f$, successive pullback gives $v^*(\pi^*(f))=(\pi v)^*(f)=u^*(f)$, hence $v^*\beta=u^*$. Likewise $\pi j=\operatorname{id}$ and $j\pi=\operatorname{id}$ give $j^*\beta=\operatorname{id}$ and $\beta j^*=\operatorname{id}$ on germs; thus $\beta$ is an isomorphism. Finally, if a nonzero $x\in k(T)$ were killed by $v^*$, applying $v^*$ to $x x^{-1}=1$ would give $0=1$ in $k(C)$, impossible. Therefore $v^*$ is injective. These are homomorphisms of fields; the argument requires no $k$-linearity for $\pi$, $\beta$ or $u^*$.

source.place: Tag 01RW (definition-function-field); pullback of germs from the definition of a scheme morphism; compare Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry/Scheme.lean, stalkMap_id and stalkMap_comp, lines 915 and 919

proof.text: If $\sigma=\operatorname{id}_k$ and $u=\operatorname{id}_C$, the constructions give $j=(\operatorname{id}_C,a)$ and $v=(\operatorname{id}_C,a)$. Thus $v=j$ and $\pi v=\operatorname{id}_C$; the canonical identity-base-change identification is $\pi$, so under it $v$ is exactly the identity.
